findings.title: Untrusted search term is concatenated into SQL, enabling injection
findings.evidence: The query now embeds the caller-provided term directly into the SQL text instead of using a bound parameter, so any input containing SQL syntax is executed as part of the statement.
findings.evidence_quote: q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%'"
findings.recommendation: Restore parameterized execution, e.g. keep the SQL as 'SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE ?' and pass the pattern as a bound argument such as '(f'%{term}%',)'.

findings.title: Search breaks for valid terms containing a single quote
findings.evidence: Because the term is inserted inside a single-quoted SQL literal, an input like O'Reilly produces invalid SQL instead of a normal search.
findings.evidence_quote: q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%'"
findings.recommendation: Use a bound parameter for the LIKE pattern so embedded quotes are escaped by the driver and valid user input does not cause syntax errors.
